title: Producing Campaign Assets at Speed

thumbnail.headline: A Week in One Session
thumbnail.image: Navy background, four stacked blocks labelled by icon (text, image, video, checkmark) next to a row of seven finished post tiles, headline in teal Inter Bold.

slide.title: A Week in One Session
slide.body: Four blocks in a row with icons: text · visuals · video · review (checkmark), leading to seven finished content tiles. Small tag: AI for Content Creators · Lesson 13 · Capstone step 2.

production_notes: [VERSION] Canva template features, CapCut templates and free-tier limits of all tools must be checked before recording.
[REGION] CapCut availability differs by country; the lesson page must name a free alternative video editor for learners where it is not available.
Noor and the handmade jewellery brand in Cairo are fictional. Stock footage of hands shaping a ring must show no real brand, shop name or logo.
Block times (50, 60, 60 and 30 minutes) come from the worked example; show them on the scene 8 to 10 slides as an example, not a target.

Hook.voiceover: Making one post at a time means opening the same tools, finding the same files and writing the same prompts, every single day. Making a whole week of content in one focused session can be much faster, if you prepare well.

Explain.voiceover: You now have a thirty-day calendar. In this lesson, you produce the first week of it. The method is batch production. That means creating many similar pieces in one working session, instead of one piece each day. It saves time, because you prepare once and stay focused on one type of task.

slide.title: Batch production
slide.body: Left, grey: one piece a day, switching tools every day. Right, teal: one session, many similar pieces, prepared once.

Explain.voiceover: Prepare three things before you start. Your voice guide, ready to paste. Your templates, in Canva for posts, quotes and tips, and in CapCut for short videos. And saved prompts, prompts that worked well before, stored in a document with blanks to fill in, such as the platform, the length and the topic.

slide.title: Prepare first
slide.body: Voice guide (Lesson 2) · Templates: Canva, CapCut (Lessons 8–9) · Saved prompt: Using the voice guide above, write a [platform] caption of about [length] words about [topic]. Hook: [type]. CTA: [action]. Give 3 variations.

Explain.voiceover: Then work in blocks, by type of task, not by day. First a text block, for all captions and emails. Then a visual block, for all the graphics. Then a video block, to film and edit the week's short video. And last, a review block, where you check everything with the five-point checklist.

slide.title: Work in blocks
slide.body: Four blocks left to right: Text → Visuals → Video → Review (5-point checklist from Lesson 10).

Explain.voiceover: As you work, keep an asset log, a spreadsheet with one row per asset. It records which tools produced which parts, which prompt you used, whether you checked the licence, and whether the asset needs a disclosure label under your rule.

slide.title: The asset log
slide.body: Table header: Asset ID · Calendar day · Channel · Asset type · Tools used · Prompt or source · AI-generated parts · Licence checked · Disclosure needed · Review status.

Explain.voiceover: Batch production is like preparing lunches for the whole week on Sunday. You wash all the vegetables at once, cook the rice once, and pack the boxes in a row. It is faster than cooking every day. But you still check that each box is fresh and correct.
Explain.stock_query: meal prep lunch boxes kitchen counter

Demonstrate.voiceover: Let's follow Noor. She runs content for a sample handmade jewellery brand in Cairo, Egypt. Days one to seven of her calendar have five feed posts, one short video and one email, across three channels.
Demonstrate.stock_query: jeweller hands shaping silver ring workshop

Demonstrate.voiceover: On Saturday morning, she works in blocks. In the text block, she uses her saved prompt and voice guide to draft all five captions and the email, with three variations each. She chooses, combines, and adds a personal sentence to each one.

slide.title: Text block · about 50 minutes
slide.body: Saved caption prompt + voice guide → 5 captions and 1 email, 3 variations each → choose, combine, add a personal sentence to each

Demonstrate.voiceover: In the visual block, she makes five graphics with her three Canva templates. Three use her own product photos, and two use AI-generated background textures. She logs the image tool and prompt for each one. In the video block, she films her hands shaping a silver ring, and edits it in CapCut with auto-captions, checking each word.

slide.title: Visual and video blocks · about 1 hour each
slide.body: 5 graphics from 3 Canva templates: 3 own product photos, 2 AI background textures (logged) · 30-second video of hands shaping a silver ring, edited in CapCut, captions checked word by word

Demonstrate.voiceover: In the review block, she places all seven assets side by side. She notices that three captions start with the same question, so she rewrites two. And the email mentions free delivery, but that offer ends before day seven. So she corrects it.

slide.title: Review block · about 30 minutes
slide.body: Seven assets side by side. Amber: 3 captions start with the same question → 2 rewritten. Red: 'free delivery' in the email, offer ends before day 7 → corrected.

Demonstrate.voiceover: Her asset log now has seven rows. For the two AI textures, disclosure needed says no, because under her rule, abstract backgrounds that do not show a realistic scene need no label. She writes the rule in the log, so a reviewer can see her reasoning.

slide.title: Noor's asset log
slide.body: Seven rows. Two AI texture rows highlighted: Disclosure needed = No · Note: 'Abstract background, not a realistic scene: no label under our disclosure rule.'

Demonstrate.voiceover: The common mistake is to rush the review, because the batch felt productive. Speed must not remove the review. In fact, batching makes review easier, because you can compare every piece side by side. Mistakes in batch work repeat. One wrong price can appear in every piece. And fill in the log as you create each asset, not later from memory.

Recap.voiceover: Let's recap. First, batch production creates a week of content in one session, by working in blocks: text, visuals, video, then review. Second, prepare your voice guide, templates and saved prompts before you start. Third, keep an asset log as you work, recording tools, prompts, licence checks and disclosure decisions for every asset.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Work in blocks: text, visuals, video, review. 2. Prepare voice guide, templates, saved prompts. 3. Log every asset as you go.

CTA.voiceover: Now it is your turn. This exercise is step two of your capstone. Produce the content for the first seven days of your campaign with Claude or ChatGPT, Canva and CapCut, and keep an asset log as you go. It takes about an hour. In the next lesson, Measuring Results and Improving with AI, we see what is working. See you there.
